fullPassage:
Living Dictionary

In 1828, an American lawyer and author Noah Webster published "An American Dictionary of the English Language" with a goal of providing America with its own version of the English language. Most dictionaries in Webster's day dictated how English words should be used rather than documenting the way people actually used English in daily life. In his dictionary, Webster broke this convention and sought to describe the way Americans spoke. When he included informal words in his dictionary, critics accused him of polluting the English language. However, Webster argued that these words captured American variations of English, distinguishing American English from British English.

With the rise of English as the world's lingua franca, there has been a movement to register English variations all over the world, for example, with the creation of the Oxford Handbook of World Englishes. Now, it is essential for English dictionaries to recognize and document words and phrases that reflect the identities and experiences of the multicultural populations who use English.

questions.passage: In 1828, an American lawyer and author Noah Webster published "An American Dictionary of the English Language" with a goal of ①<u>providing</u> America with its own version. Most dictionaries in Webster's day ②<u>dictated</u> how English words should be used rather than documenting the way people actually used English. In his dictionary, Webster broke this convention and ③<u>sought</u> to describe the way Americans ④<u>speaking</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 미국인들이 말하는 방식. 과거시제 spoke 필요.
det.analysis: ✅ ①providing: of + V-ing, 정상. ✅ ②dictated: 과거시제, 정상. ✅ ③sought: seek의 과거형, 정상. ❌ ④speaking: 'the way Americans spoke'에서 과거시제 spoke 필요. speaking은 시제 불일치.
det.tip: the way + S + V(과거): ~가 ~한 방식. spoke(과거) vs speaking(현재분사).

questions.passage: When he included informal words in his dictionary, critics accused him of ①<u>polluting</u> the English language. However, Webster ②<u>argued</u> that these words captured American variations of English, ③<u>distinguishing</u> American English from British English. With the rise of English as the world's lingua franca, there has been a movement ④<u>registering</u> English variations all over the world.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 영어 변형을 등록하려는 움직임. a movement to register 필요.
det.analysis: ✅ ①polluting: accuse A of V-ing, 정상. ✅ ②argued: 과거시제, 정상. ✅ ③distinguishing: 분사구문, 정상. ❌ ④registering: a movement to V(to부정사) 필요. a movement to register가 맞음.
det.tip: a movement to V: ~하려는 운동. to register (O) / registering (X).

questions.passage: Most dictionaries in Webster's day dictated how English words should be used rather than ①<u>documenting</u> the way people actually used English. Webster broke this convention. When he included informal words, critics ②<u>accused</u> him of polluting English. However, Webster argued that these words captured American variations, distinguishing American English from British English. Now, it is essential for dictionaries to recognize words ③<u>what</u> reflect the identities of the multicultural populations ④<u>who</u> use English.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 정체성을 반영하는 단어들. 선행사 words가 있으므로 that 필요.
det.analysis: ✅ ①documenting: rather than + V-ing, 정상. ✅ ②accused: accuse A of B, 정상. ❌ ③what: 선행사 words가 있으므로 관계대명사 that/which 필요. what은 선행사 포함이므로 불가. ✅ ④who: populations who, 주격 관계대명사, 정상.
det.tip: words that reflect (O) / words what reflect (X). what = the thing(s) that. 선행사 있으면 what 불가.

questions.passage: In 1828, Noah Webster published "An American Dictionary of the English Language" with a goal of providing America with its own version. Most dictionaries in his day ①<u>dictated</u> how English words should be used rather than ②<u>documenting</u> the way people actually used English. In his dictionary, Webster ③<u>maintained</u> this convention and sought to describe the way Americans spoke. When he included informal words, critics ④<u>accused</u> him of polluting the English language.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 웹스터는 이 관행을 깨뜨렸다(broke). maintained(유지했다)는 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ①dictated: 원문 그대로. ✅ ②documenting: 원문 그대로. ❌ ③maintained(유지했다): 원문은 broke(깨뜨렸다). 관행을 '유지'한 것이 아니라 '깨뜨린' 것. ✅ ④accused: 원문 그대로.
det.tip: broke(깨뜨렸다) ↔ maintained(유지했다). 웹스터는 관행에 반기를 든 혁신자.

questions.passage: However, Webster argued that these words captured American ①<u>variations</u> of English, distinguishing American English from British English. With the ②<u>rise</u> of English as the world's lingua franca, there has been a movement to register English variations. Now, it is essential for English dictionaries to ③<u>recognize</u> and document words that ④<u>conceal</u> the identities and experiences of the multicultural populations who use English.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 다문화 인구의 정체성을 반영하는(reflect) 단어. conceal(숨기다)은 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ①variations: 원문 그대로. ✅ ②rise: 원문 그대로. ✅ ③recognize: 원문 그대로. ❌ ④conceal(숨기다): 원문은 reflect(반영하다). 정체성을 '숨기는' 게 아니라 '반영하는' 것.
det.tip: reflect(반영하다) ↔ conceal(숨기다, 감추다).

questions.passage:
Living Dictionary

In 1828, an American lawyer and author Noah Webster published "An American Dictionary of the English Language" with a goal of providing America with its own version of the English language. Most dictionaries in Webster's day dictated how English words should be used rather than documenting the way people actually used English in daily life. In his dictionary, Webster broke this convention and sought to describe the way Americans spoke. When he included informal words in his dictionary, ____. However, Webster argued that these words captured American variations of English, distinguishing American English from British English.

With the rise of English as the world's lingua franca, there has been a movement to register English variations all over the world, for example, with the creation of the Oxford Handbook of World Englishes. Now, it is essential for English dictionaries to recognize and document words and phrases that reflect the identities and experiences of the multicultural populations who use English.

questions.passage:
Living Dictionary

In 1828, an American lawyer and author Noah Webster published "An American Dictionary of the English Language" with a goal of providing America with its own version of the English language. Most dictionaries in Webster's day dictated how English words should be used rather than documenting the way people actually used English in daily life. In his dictionary, Webster broke this convention and sought to describe the way Americans spoke. When he included informal words in his dictionary, critics accused him of polluting the English language. However, Webster argued that these words captured American variations of English, distinguishing American English from British English.

With the rise of English as the world's lingua franca, there has been a movement to register English variations all over the world, for example, with the creation of the Oxford Handbook of World Englishes. Now, it is essential for English dictionaries to recognize and document words and phrases that reflect the identities and experiences of the multicultural populations who use English.
